assertionResults.reason: GitHub stayed mode-aware and unready: the repo-bound env-only CLI status remained `needs_attention` with missing-token repair guidance, while the browser account page overlaid shared-scope denial instead of ever surfacing a false ready state for the hidden `hack-cli` project.

The GitHub surface exposed the active profile (`default`), routing source (`implicit_default`), token mode, installation state (`not required`), and explicit repair actions for both missing token access and refreshing hidden shared scope.

Linear clearly separated machine-local usability from broker-backed/shared visibility: the disposable session had no visible broker connection and no local env token, so the browser showed `Connected on Hack: not connected`, `Local access: needs repair`, hid the connected account by scope, and pointed repair at `hack auth login` for the hidden shared project path.

The Linear binding view stayed accurate and deduplicated: browser and CLI both showed the active `default` profile, the same default Hack project binding, zero additional linked projects, and no duplicate project entries.

Status-update publishing and delivery reconciliation remained auditable across CLI, browser, and repo files: the browser mirrored the latest published update metadata and the `processed/applied/failed` counts from repo-bound Linear status, and the copied published markdown plus `delivery-audit.json` matched those values exactly.

The disposable account's shared-scope visibility stayed fail-closed across surfaces: broker APIs returned no visible projects and `project_not_found` for `hack-cli`, the browser defaulted to the only visible org/team and clamped both integration sections to `Shared project scope denied for hack-cli`, and the matching isolated CLI session never inferred usable shared ownership or integration access for that hidden project.

frictions.description: Shell TLS trust for the routed local hosts was not configured for non-browser tools, so curl checks required `-k` and the isolated CLI evidence used `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` with the routed auth host.
frictions.resolution: Used the already-running routed hosts with explicit insecure-local transport flags instead of mutating global trust settings.

frictions.description: The mission guidance pointed at `http://127.0.0.1:8080`, but that broker endpoint was unreachable from this worker.
frictions.resolution: Fell back to the routed auth host `https://auth.hack-cli.hack`, which served the same broker/auth APIs successfully for curl, browser bridge, and isolated CLI checks.

frictions.description: `agent-browser network requests` did not retain the already-settled server-rendered page load, so browser-side request capture came back empty after navigation settled.
frictions.resolution: Used direct `curl` captures against the broker APIs for request/response evidence and kept the browser evidence focused on rendered UI plus console cleanliness.

summary: Tested 6 assigned assertions and all 6 passed. The hidden-scope disposable account proved that the browser integration surfaces fail closed against broker project visibility while still exposing accurate GitHub/Linear routing, repair, binding, and repo audit details from the repo-bound CLI state.
